hook: The rulebook for who owns a listing just moved — and the listing system can now claim a share of it.
market_map: Today: the Realtor group lets local listing systems claim up to half the copyright in listing content. Its data chief warns agents about AI, and Agentree launches an AI studio that clones an agent's voice.

stories.title: The Realtor group lets local listing systems claim up to half the copyright in listing content
stories.summary: On Nov 8, the Realtor group's board approved four listing-system policy changes. The headline one is optional for each local listing system. It may make brokers who don't opt out hand over up to a 50% shared copyright stake in listing photos and marketing materials. That is shared ownership, not ownership of half the photos — and no listing system has adopted it yet.

sources.label: Approved Nov 8 at NAR NXT, reported Nov 9

stories.title: The national Realtor group's data chief warns agents about AI — and the numbers show why now
stories.summary: At the national Realtor group's annual meeting on November 8, its data chief Mike Woodward warned agents about AI. Free AI tools take in what you feed them, and they invent facts with confidence — even as 23% of agents now use them daily. He asked Claude for records on his own home, and five of seven facts came back wrong. His rule: show the original, label the edit, and confess.

stories.title: Agentree launches AI Studio — the whole listing-marketing job in one browser tab, cloned voice included
stories.summary: Agentree launched AI Studio on November 10. One browser tab does headshots, virtual staging, video walkthroughs, and talking videos in the agent's own cloned voice. The free plan includes a website and 30 AI credits; Pro is $69 a month. But the release says nothing about disclosing AI-altered photos or marking AI-made images, with disclosure laws taking effect January 1, 2027.

watch.title: Copyright + data-feed policy — no adopter yet.
watch.text: Approved Nov 8: a local listing system may claim up to a 50% shared copyright interest in listing content, and set its own data-feed rules. No listing system has adopted it yet — watch for the first one.

watch.title: Tuccori buyer settlement — STILL no outcome, 8 days after the hearing.
watch.text: The Nov 2 fairness hearing ended with the court still deciding; a tracker checked Nov 9 confirms no order since. Do not cite approval. $120.3M fund, 132,000+ claims, 25 opt-outs, 2 objections.

watch.title: AI photo disclosure — hard deadline Jan 1, 2027 (52 days).
watch.text: California's rental-ad disclosure law and Wisconsin's ad rule take effect Jan 1, 2027. The Realtor group's own annual meeting now preaches the same rule. One Wisconsin listing system has enforced it since Sept 1 — $10 a day for an unlabeled altered main photo.

watch.title: Compass fight — no new movement in-window.
watch.text: Nov 3–4 press still recaps the Oct 30 items: a seventh plaintiff joined, and Compass plans to ask the court to dismiss the case. No trial date yet in either case.

watch.title: The Realtor group's annual meeting ended Nov 8, New Orleans.
watch.text: The copyright and data-feed policies are the real outcome here. The Open Real Estate vendor pick still runs through Q1 2027.
